# PR #3109: Patch: an acceptance test holds the pure crates' thread-locals and mutable statics to the list rule 4 allows

Closes #3063

Acceptance now has a check that fails when a pure crate declares a static that CLAUDE.md rule 4 doesn't allow. I added it to `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs`, the only file changed, and it passes on today's tree. I followed the issue's plan and pasted its prototype code as written. I made no code departures.

**What it does**
- `RULE_4_STATICS` lists the four statics rule 4 allows: `FOLDING` and `POOL_HOLD` in `crates/engine/src/catalog.rs`, `HOST` in `crates/engine/src/custom.rs`, and `VM` in `crates/luau/src/vm.rs`. Its comment points at rule 4 and R767000, R915002 and R2201001.
- The scan covers `crates/{engine,cards,ai,luau,run}/src`, reading source text as the other acceptance scans do.
- It skips `src/testkit/`, out-of-line test files (`tests.rs`, `*_tests.rs`) and any item after an exact `#[cfg(test)]`. `#[cfg(any(test, …))]` stays read, because it compiles outside tests.
- It flags every `thread_local!` static, every `static mut` and every static whose type names `Cell`, `RefCell`, `UnsafeCell` or an `Atomic*` type. `OnceLock` and `LazyLock` statics pass.
- The failure message says to change rule 4 and `RULE_4_STATICS` in one pull request, or take the static out.
- A header bullet in the file's `//!` list names the check.

**Tests added** (all four in `acceptance.rs`, so they run in the `tools, wasm` group)
- `statics_the_pure_crates_hold_only_the_statics_rule_4_allows` runs the real tree against `RULE_4_STATICS`.
- `statics_the_scan_finds_each_interior_static` is a text-scan test. It flags `thread_local!` in both brace and paren forms, `static mut`, `AtomicU32`, `[AtomicBool; 2]`, `&[AtomicU8]` and `Cell`. It leaves `OnceLock`, a `LazyLock` whose initializer calls `Cell::new`, `[GridCell; 2]`, `'static` lifetimes, `static_flags` and `Static::new` alone.
- `statics_the_scan_skips_test_items_and_keeps_the_lines` checks the `#[cfg(test)]` skip and that line numbers survive it.
- `statics_the_check_refuses_an_unlisted_static_in_each_pure_crate` plants files in a scratch root for each of the five crates, like the helper check's scratch test.
  - A `thread_local!`, an `AtomicU32` static and a `static mut` are reported with file and line.
  - A `OnceLock` static, a `thread_local!` inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, one under `src/testkit/` and one in `walk_tests.rs` are not.
  - The failure message names rule 4 and `RULE_4_STATICS`.
  - An allow-list entry clears its static, and an entry naming nothing is reported as stale.

**Commands run**
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test acceptance statics_` passed 4 of 4.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test acceptance` passed 35 of 35, so V23's reader scan and the daily-ignore scan don't object to the new text.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` were clean.
- `cargo jackioh spec check` printed `1703 rulings, 4160 proofs, 51341 citations in 3289 files, 21896 links: ok`.
- `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` printed `classify: Internal`.
- I did not run the workspace-wide cargo tests, web tests or catalog and patches checks; the diff touches only a tools test file.

**Decisions the issue left open**
- **Stale entries fail too.** An allow-list entry whose static no longer exists is reported, so rule 4 and the list can't drift apart. The rejected alternative was a pure deny-check. Renaming `FOLDING`, for example, now fails until `RULE_4_STATICS` and rule 4 change together.
- **`Mutex` and `RwLock` statics aren't flagged**, because `clippy.toml` already bans them.
- **`#[cfg(test)]` is skipped item by item**, not by cutting the file at the first one as `config_code` does. A cut would hide a static declared after a `#[cfg(test)] use` in `crates/cards/src/lib.rs`.
- **Out-of-line test modules are skipped by file name** (`tests.rs`, `*_tests.rs`), because `crates/run/src/lib.rs` declares those under `#[cfg(test)]`.

**What a reviewer should look at twice**
- It reads source text, not a parse, so its blind spots are the ones named in the plan's risks section.
  - A string literal spelling `static X: Cell<…>` is flagged, which fails loudly.
  - An unbalanced brace inside a string within a `#[cfg(test)]` item can end the skip early or late. Early shows up as a loud flag. Late could hide a static after that item, but test modules are last in these files.
  - A spaced-out `thread_local ! {` is missed, and rustfmt never produces it.
- I did not touch `CLAUDE.md`, any `clippy.toml`, `crates/tools/README.md` (it lists no acceptance checks) or `scripts/ci-scope.sh` (every pure crate's `src` already turns on `rust_tools_wasm`).
